newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says France economy improving, except jobs.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says France economy improving, except jobs.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe, battling a slump in public support, said on Sunday that France's economy was improving on all fronts apart from jobs.

"I'm perfectly aware that the situation today in France is difficult," Juppe told the Progres de Lyon regional daily in an interview to be published on Monday when asked about a one-day strike by civil servants last week against austerity policies.

"I'd like to recall that the situation is getting better on every front except for unemployment -- prices, foreign trade, inflation, interest rates, currency. Growth rose one percent in the third quarter."

He added: "The reforms which we have undertaken with the French people will enable us to face the future with the maximum of trump cards. That's why I'm sending a message, not of smug optimism, but of confidence."
Opinion polls say record unemployment, at 12.6 percent of the workforce, is the over-riding concern of the French people.
A poll on Sunday said public supoprt for conservative Juppe had tumbled to its lowest level since he took office in May 1995 on a short-lived wave of enthusiasm.
The IFOP survey for the Journal du Dimanche newspaper said only 21 percent of voters were happy with Juppe as premier, down from 27 percent in September.

Juppe said there was no "generalised depression" in France. Many of the people he met in Paris and on trips around the country "believe that we are going in the right direction, that we should keep going."

He reiterated government figures that only one in three civil servants took part in Thursday's one-day strike against job cuts and austerity policies aimed at enabling France to qualify for a single currency from 1999.
The strike, the first big demonstration of union power since a crippling 24-day wave of stoppages late last year, hit planes, schools, trains and other public services.
